Header: 2026-06-07 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Riley (Redwood Partnerships), Sanjay (Polaris Head of Partnerships), Lena (Polaris Cloud), Tom (CTO), Asha (BD)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro, explore integration patterns, surface security and deployment constraints, agree next steps for pilot and technical deep dive.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — super excited. Quick round of intros?
[00:08] Sanjay: Yeah hi, Sanjay Rao, Head of Partnerships at Polaris Edge. We run partnerships and marketplace integrations, we have a managed GPU cloud offering in NA and EU.
[00:17] Lena: Lena Ortiz, Cloud Solutions. I look after infra and devops for partner integrations.
[00:22] Tom: Tom Becker, CTO, driving our ML platform and partner tech.
[00:27] Maya: Awesome, I'm Maya Patel, AE at Redwood. With me is Ethan Li, our systems engineer, and Riley from partnerships.
[00:34] Ethan: Hey all.
[00:36] Asha: Asha Menon, Business Dev, hi.

[00:40] Maya: Cool. The goal today is to understand where Polaris sees value working with Redwood — resell, managed offering, marketplace listing, and any technical blockers. We'll surface security/compliance and pilot ideas.
[00:52] Sanjay: High level, we want to offer customers a turn-key inference service with multiple model options and predictable pricing. We're exploring both a reseller arrangement where we resell Redwood Dedicated capacity and a tighter integration where we host Redwood Private in our VPC and offer it as a managed add-on.
[01:12] Maya: Makes sense. Two common patterns: 1) Marketplace/resell — Polaris can resell Redwood hosted or Dedicated capacity with partner margins, and we handle infra; 2) Private deployment — Redwood Private or a VPC-managed deployment where you control networking and keys. Do you have a preference?
[01:31] Lena: From infra POV, private deployments are attractive but we need to understand network requirements — VPC peering vs PrivateLink, NAT, egress, and whether we can run a small on-prem or VPC control plane.
[01:45] Ethan: Quick note — Redwood Private supports VPC peering and a control plane option. Our runtime can sit in customer VPCs, and for multi-tenant we can do dedicated GPU pools. For benchmarks we usually recommend a 3-node Dedicated pool for initial tests; it gives predictable throughput.
[02:03] Tom: What's the story on key management and encryption? Our customers require CMEK and HSM integration.
[02:11] Maya: We support KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed keys. HSM is supported via key wrapping patterns; we'll share the security pack with implementation details.
[02:23] Asha: On the commercial side, how do margins look for resellers? Do you have a partner program slide?
[02:30] Riley: Yes, partner program deck has margin tiers based on committed capacity. We'll send the partner one-pager and deck after this call.

[02:40] Sanjay: A few engineering questions — latency SLOs, batching behavior, and how model variant fallbacks work for capacity constrained times.
[02:49] Ethan: Our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache — sorry 'KV cash' — our transcription has that wrong — but basically prefix caching. For latency SLOs we can route by policy, so low latency routes can hit smaller batch sizes or dedicated pools. For fallbacks, we can automatically route to smaller or quantized variants if the requested variant isn't available.
[03:12] Lena: For VPC deployments, does traffic leave the VPC for model weights or can we pre-stage weights in caches?
[03:20] Ethan: You can pre-stage model weights on the serving nodes in your region; nothing needs to egress to public endpoints once provisioned. For supervised updates we sync through the control plane over peered network.

[03:35] Tom: How much effort is integration? Our infra team expects a runbook.
[03:40] Maya: We'll provide an integration runbook and an infra diagram. Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks to provision a test Dedicated pool, run benchmarks, and validate telemetry + billing integration.
[03:52] Sanjay: Telemetry — what do you expose? We want token-level cost estimates and per-model latency.
[03:59] Ethan: We expose per-request telemetry, token counts, latency histograms, per-model dashboards. We also have hooks for tracing and can push to your observability backends.

[04:12] Lena: Authentication — SSO / SAML support? We need RBAC integrated into our portal so customers can self-serve.
[04:20] Maya: SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported for the console. For API keys we integrate with your identity provider for service accounts and can tie to RBAC. We'll outline best practices in the security pack.

[04:33] Asha: A couple of go-to-market questions: will Redwood be OK with joint case studies, logos, and co-marketing?
[04:40] Riley: Absolutely. We encourage co-marketing for strategic partners. There's a partner marketing kit we'll include.

[04:47] Sanjay: On procurement/legal — we'll need standard MSA, data processing addendum, and evidence of SOC2 Type II. Do you have those?
[04:56] Maya: Yes, we'll share the SOC2 report and DPA; for private deployments we can offer an enterprise agreement. We'll also share our SOC2 redacted artifacts in the security pack.

[05:06] Tom: Let's talk about a pilot scope — we want to validate throughput for our customers: target 95th percentile latency < 120ms for conversational models at 128 tokens and cost per call targets.
[05:18] Ethan: For that SLA we'd recommend Dedicated capacity and specific kernel/quantization profiles. We'll include recommended instance types and quantization suggestions. The pilot benchmark will measure p95 latency, throughput, and cost per token across a small workload (10k sample requests).

[05:33] Lena: For networking, we'll need an approved IP allowlist and probably PrivateLink for cross-account access.
[05:40] Ethan: PrivateLink is on our roadmap; VPC peering is supported today. We'll capture that in the tech deep dive.

[05:48] Asha: Timeline — our procurement cycle is about 6 weeks. Could we run a pilot in parallel?
[05:55] Maya: Yes, pilots can start before procurement closes; we do an MOU for pilots. Typical pilot is 2-6 weeks.

[06:02] Sanjay: Any notable customers or references?
[06:05] Riley: We can share references in regulated verticals and case studies about Dedicated deployments for latency-sensitive apps.

[06:12] Tom: One last technical detail — model updates and compatibility. How do you handle model version pinning?
[06:18] Ethan: Customers can pin model versions and configure rollouts. We also provide automatic fallback policies and can stage rollouts for Canary or A/B tests.

[06:28] Maya: Great — to recap next steps: we'll send partner deck, security pack, and a proposed pilot scope and benchmark plan. Polaris will share VPC/network requirements and timeline. We'll schedule a technical deep dive the week of June 21.
[06:43] Sanjay: Sounds good.
[06:45] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[06:47] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links.
